issues.on_page: Schedule A prints the codes 1100-5690 as one 'Local Sources' list with no 'Other Local Receipts' group or subtotal
issues.issue: The split is not printed in the report: it was inferred because these six Schedule A lines happen to add up to 1,585,717.45. That is exactly what the rule 'never split a line just because some other statement's lines add up to it' forbids. The amounts are exact (sum 1,585,717.45). Keep it as one printed line with review 'broad group; detail on p5', or get a person to approve the code-range split.

Same kind of inferred split, but this line is made up entirely of taxes, and the combined-tax-line rule allows splitting from a budget schedule. The arithmetic is exact. Defensible but needs a person to confirm.

The page says the source: other school districts, which are local governments. That fits intergovernmental/state aid (detail: county/other local governments), the category used for the parallel line 1960 Miscellaneous Revenue - Other Local Governments. 'other' is a last resort and shouldn't be used here. Same for detail[10].category/detail_category (other / miscellaneous revenue).
The receipt-category rules name nameplate capacity tax explicitly under 'other taxes' (detail 'other local taxes'). Small amount, but it contradicts the rule.
Labels of the split receipt lines (receipts[0]-[2], [5]-[10]) have ' (within ...)' appended, so original_label isn't exactly as printed. The parent line is already recorded in split_from.

OK as charges for services (Exhibit II shows it as Charges for Services). The detail lines are 'tuition and fees', but they are contracted SPED/education services billed to districts, so 'other charges for services' would also fit. Judgment call.
